developers.name: Derek Yoo
developers.activity: Founder and CEO of Moonbeam (PureStake). Former VP of Engineering at Fuze (acquired by Thinkingphones, later Mitel), where he scaled cloud telephony infrastructure for enterprise customers. Leading the Moonbeam parachain integration with the Polkadot Relay Chain, the EVM compatibility layer on Substrate, and the cross-chain GMP messaging architecture that anchors the platform's multichain pitch.

developers.name: Stefan Mehlhorn
developers.activity: Chief Operating Officer of PureStake/Moonbeam. Former operations executive at multiple enterprise software companies. Leading ecosystem partner onboarding, the Moonbeam Foundation governance rollout, and the launch of the Moonriver canary network on Kusama that preceded the Moonbeam parachain auction win on Polkadot.

developers.name: PureStake Engineering Team
developers.activity: 30+ engineer team running validator infrastructure for Polkadot, Algorand, and the Moonbeam parachain. Driving the moonbeam-runtime Substrate code (Rust), the Ethereum compatibility precompiles, and the XCM cross-chain messaging integration that allows assets to move between Moonbeam, the Polkadot Relay Chain, and sister parachains like Acala and Astar.

narrativeAtSnapshot: Moonbeam is an EVM-compatible smart contract parachain on the Polkadot relay chain, built on the Substrate framework and developed by the Boston-based PureStake team. The platform won the second Polkadot parachain auction in November 2021, securing a 96-week lease backed by approximately 35 million DOT (worth roughly $1.4 billion at the auction's peak) contributed by 200,000+ crowdloan participants who received GLMR rewards in proportion to their DOT lockups. The Moonbeam mainnet launched in production phase on January 11, 2022 — two days before the snapshot — and is rapidly onboarding its first EVM-native DeFi protocols including StellaSwap, BeamSwap, and Solarbeam, along with announced integrations with Chainlink, The Graph, and Sushi. The pitch is structurally clean: Polkadot's shared-security model gives Moonbeam validator security from the Relay Chain's nominator set without bootstrapping its own validator economy, while EVM compatibility allows the protocol to inherit the entire Ethereum tooling stack (Solidity, MetaMask, Hardhat, Foundry, Etherscan-equivalents) without forcing developers to learn Substrate's Rust runtime. The team is execution-focused: Derek Yoo previously scaled cloud telephony at Fuze through enterprise integrations, and PureStake's 30-engineer infrastructure team has run Polkadot validators since the network's genesis. The narrative environment is favorable: Polkadot launched its first parachains in December 2021 amidst intense market enthusiasm for the relay-chain multichain thesis, and GLMR's $14.50 listing price reflects the substantial crowdloan deposit value. The bear case is fundamental. The Polkadot DeFi ecosystem is a fraction of Ethereum mainnet ($150B TVL) or even Binance Smart Chain ($16B TVL): the combined TVL across all Polkadot parachains is under $1B at snapshot, with no single application of meaningful global scale. Cross-chain messaging via XCM remains in early production, and the integration overhead for new protocols is significant. EVM compatibility is no longer a differentiator — Avalanche, Polygon, Fantom, and BNB Chain all offer EVM with deeper liquidity and larger user bases, and the cost advantage of Moonbeam over a deployed Ethereum L2 like Arbitrum or Optimism is not obvious. GLMR's tokenomics include a 5% perpetual inflation schedule that creates persistent dilution; the parachain slot lease expires in 96 weeks, requiring either a successful re-bid (significant DOT cost) or relegation. The shared-security model that anchors the bull case also creates fundamental dependency on DOT's price and validator participation — Moonbeam cannot survive a Polkadot relay chain reorganization or hard fork that goes adversely. The team raised only $6M in seed funding (September 2020) — modest compared to L1 competitors. Most critically, the structural question facing all Polkadot parachains is whether developers and users will choose Polkadot's deliberately slower, more conservative architecture over the rollup-centric Ethereum future where modular L2s offer comparable scalability with native access to Ethereum's liquidity and security.
